subject.name: Bhakti Charu Swami
subject.lede: Six chapters — from a village in Bengal to the lotus feet of Śrīla Prabhupāda, and a lifetime spent giving away what he received there. Scroll to walk through them, or jump to any chapter.

eras.title: A Son of Bengal
eras.subtitle: Kuti to Kolkata
eras.theme: Born into an aristocratic Bengali family in a quiet village of East Bengal, and raised in a Kolkata that took almost everything back — a boyhood that gave him the mother tongue he would one day fill with his guru’s words.

events.title: Born at Kuti, in the district of Brahmanbaria
events.body: He appears in this world on the 17th of September 1945, in an aristocratic Bengali family of the village of Kuti, in the Brahmanbaria district of what was then the Bengal Presidency. In later years he would return to this same soil to establish a temple, so that the place of his birth might become a place of the holy name.

events.title: A fortune dissolves in Kolkata
events.body: Most of his childhood is spent in the city. While he is still a boy his mother is taken by a contagious disease and the household falls from its old wealth into poverty — an aristocratic family’s fortune dissolving before the eyes of a child who wanted only his mother. After his basic schooling he leaves home altogether, in search of adventure, friendship and a better life.

eras.title: The Search
eras.subtitle: Chemistry, the Himālayas, and a book he did not ask for
eras.theme: Six years of looking — in a German university, in the West, and along the Himālayas — before the shelter he was searching for was placed into his hands in his own city.

events.title: Leaves India to study in Germany
events.body: In pursuit of higher education he leaves India for Germany, where he attends university and studies chemistry. There, alongside his studies, he begins to research the ancient Vedic scriptures — and in time grows dissatisfied with the culture he had travelled so far to join.

events.title: A year in the Himālayas, and no one to surrender to
events.body: In 1975 he returns to India to pursue the spiritual path wholeheartedly, and for a year he travels the Himālayan region of the north in search of a genuine spiritual master. The search is extensive but fruitless — he finds no one to whom he can fully surrender. Despondent and empty-handed, he comes back to Kolkata in 1976.

events.title: He asks for a Gītā and is given the Nectar of Devotion
events.body: A visit from his old friend Prasun — by then Sarvabhāvana Dāsa of the Kolkata temple — brings him through ISKCON’s doors. After a few visits he asks to buy a copy of Bhagavad-gītā; the temple has none on hand, and what he is given instead is Śrīla Prabhupāda’s rendering of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī’s Nectar of Devotion. That book, he said, completely changed his life.

events.title: He joins the devotees at Śrīdhāma Māyāpur
events.body: In the second half of 1976 he joins ISKCON at Śrīdhāma Māyāpur, the birthplace of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. The search of six years ends where śaraṇāgati begins — in the association of devotees.

eras.title: At Prabhupāda’s Side
eras.subtitle: One year that decided a lifetime
eras.theme: Eleven months in the personal service of His Divine Grace A. C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda — one order received, two initiations, sannyāsa, and a vigil kept to the very end.

image.alt: His Holiness Bhakti Charu Swami Maharaja with folded hands
image.caption: In the shelter of his spiritual master.

events.title: First meeting, at the Kumbha-melā
events.body: Brought before Śrīla Prabhupāda by Bhavānanda Mahārāja at the Kumbha-melā, he meets the spiritual master he had crossed continents to find. At that first meeting Śrīla Prabhupāda asks him to translate all of his books into Bengali, accepts him into his personal entourage, and appoints him secretary for Indian affairs — and his personal servant and cook.

quote.text: You translate my books into Bengali.
quote.source: Śrīla Prabhupāda to Bhakti Charu Swami, Kumbha-melā, January 1977

events.title: First and second initiation, on Gaura-pūrṇimā
events.body: During the Gaura-pūrṇimā festival at Māyāpur, Śrīla Prabhupāda gives him both harināma and brāhmaṇa initiation together — the formal beginning of a relationship that had already been sealed in the heart.

events.title: The watch from twelve to two
events.body: At Rishikesh, where Śrīla Prabhupāda has gone for his health, Maharaja attends him each day from twelve to two o’clock. It is in one of those hours that his spiritual master tells him what must be done next.

quote.text: The time has come for me to die, and I want to die in Vṛndāvana. So make arrangements to take me to Vṛndāvana.
quote.source: Śrīla Prabhupāda to Bhakti Charu Swami, Rishikesh, 1977 — as recounted by devotees who served with him

events.title: Sannyāsa, from his spiritual master’s own hand
events.body: On the 29th of May 1977, at the Snāna-yātrā season in Vṛndāvana, Śrīla Prabhupāda awards him the renounced order of life — and with it the name by which the world would come to know him.

events.title: In his spiritual master’s kitchen
events.body: Through the Vṛndāvana months he cooks for Śrīla Prabhupāda in his personal kitchen and massages him, one of the very few devotees permitted so close to his person. Eleven months of that association were all he was given; godbrothers would say afterwards that in them he had absorbed his spiritual master’s very spirit. He had come looking for a guru to surrender to, and was allowed instead to feed him.

events.title: Śrīla Prabhupāda departs this world
events.body: He remains in Śrīla Prabhupāda’s personal service to the last, in the room at Krishna-Balaram Mandir where his spiritual master leaves this world surrounded by chanting disciples. In less than a single year he had received everything; the remaining forty-three would be spent giving it away.

eras.title: A Promise Kept
eras.subtitle: Fifty volumes in his mother tongue
eras.theme: One instruction, received at a first meeting, carried out over almost twenty years — until every major book of Śrīla Prabhupāda stood complete in Bengali, in time for his centennial.

events.title: The Book Trust at Kolkata and Māyāpura
events.body: In the years after his spiritual master’s departure he serves at Śrīdhāma Māyāpur, while the society passes through a critical phase, and takes a leading role in establishing the Bhaktivedanta Book Trust at Kolkata and Māyāpura — the press that would carry his translations across Bengal.

events.title: Volume by volume, page by page
events.body: Year after year the work goes on: Bhagavad-gītā As It Is, Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta and much besides. For almost twenty years this rendering was his primary service. It was the service his spiritual master had given him, and so there was never a question of doing anything else.

image.alt: Bhakti Charu Swami Maharaja at work translating
image.caption: The service of a lifetime, one page at a time.

events.title: Initiating spiritual master and GBC member
events.body: In 1987 he begins to accept disciples as an initiating spiritual master within ISKCON and joins the Governing Body Commission, the society’s ultimate managing authority. He would serve as its chairman in 1989, and again twenty-eight years later, in 2017.

events.title: Abhay Charan
events.body: In 1995 he embarks on the writing, production and direction of an epic video serial on the life and teachings of Śrīla Prabhupāda, drawn from Śrīla Prabhupāda-līlāmṛta. Its first episode airs on Indian national television on the seventh of September 1996 — the day after his spiritual master’s centennial appearance day — and week by week, in episodes of twenty-five minutes, it carries that story into millions of homes.

image.alt: Bhakti Charu Swami Maharaja directing the Abhay Charan television series
image.caption: Directing Abhay Charan — Prabhupāda’s life, told to a nation.

events.title: The centennial — the work complete
events.body: For the hundredth anniversary of Śrīla Prabhupāda’s appearance the instruction received at that first meeting in January 1977 is fulfilled and laid at his feet: all of his major works stand rendered into Bengali, more than fifty volumes in all. In the same year he establishes the Veda Foundation, to carry Vedic knowledge further still.

eras.title: Temples, Kitchens and Kīrtana
eras.subtitle: Ujjain, and everywhere else
eras.theme: Deities installed, children fed, the sick treated, and the songs of the ācāryas set down in his own voice — the same surrender, now expressed in marble, rice and sound.

events.title: The temple at Ujjain
events.body: In the ancient city where Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma studied at the school of Sāndīpani Muni, he raises a marble temple for Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Madana-mohana, Kṛṣṇa-Balarāma, Gaura-Nitāi, Jagannātha-Baladeva-Subhadrā and Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva — begun at the invitation of the Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh and completed, astonishingly, in some ten months. He serves as the resident GBC for the region.

events.title: A kitchen for twenty-three thousand children
events.body: Beside the temple stands a six-thousand-square-foot kitchen from which more than twenty-three thousand schoolchildren are fed sanctified food every single day. He is later entrusted with the chairmanship of the Annamṛta Foundation, ISKCON’s midday-meal programme, which carries the same pattern to more than a million schoolchildren across India. It is preaching of the plainest kind: no child needs a translation of a plate of prasādam.

events.title: Four mornings on Śaraṇāgati
events.body: At Ujjain he gives a seminar on Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura’s Śaraṇāgati, taking the six limbs of surrender song by song across successive mornings. He treats the songs not as performance but as instruction — translating line by line, having the devotees repeat each refrain until it is theirs. In Bhaktivinoda’s verses, he explains, one is hearing the very mood of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

events.title: The songs, set down in his own voice
events.body: Renowned for the sweetness of his singing, he sets down over these years a body of recordings — Śaraṇāgati, selected songs of the Vaiṣṇava poets, Gītār Gān, the Abhay Charan soundtrack — and year after year takes his turn leading the mahā-mantra at the Kīrtana Melā in Māyāpur before thousands of devotees. He sang as he translated: slowly, plainly, and for whoever was listening. It is by this voice, more than by anything else, that most of the world still comes to him.

events.title: Panihati, and a temple at his birthplace
events.body: He oversees the development of the temple at Panihati in northern Kolkata — the sacred place of the daṇḍa-mahotsava of Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu. In these same later years he also establishes a temple at Kuti in Bangladesh, the village where he was born.

events.title: Ārogya Niketan, and the Artha Forum
events.body: He establishes the Ārogya Niketan Āyurvedic clinic at Ujjain, and joins the Artha Forum, speaking to business leaders on spirituality and the purpose of wealth.

events.title: Ocean of Mercy — a search fulfilled
events.body: He writes down at last his own remembrances of Śrīla Prabhupāda: how a young man’s long search was fulfilled, and how love for his spiritual master grew in him. On the 17th of November that same year the Institute of International Social Development of New York — an organisation holding consultative status with the United Nations Economic and Social Council — honours him for his work.

events.title: A cow sanctuary in Florida
events.body: He establishes the Veda Foundation’s temple, farm community and cow sanctuary on a hundred and twenty acres at DeLand, Florida — simple living and high thinking, on the far side of the world from Kuti. The year before, in 2017, he had served once more as chairman of the GBC.

eras.title: Return to the Eternal
eras.subtitle: 4 July 2020
eras.theme: A worldwide family chanting for his health around the clock; and then, on a summer morning in America, the departure of a devotee whose whole life had been the practice of surrender.

events.title: Placed on a ventilator in Florida
events.body: Soon after arriving in Florida he falls ill and tests positive for COVID-19. On the 17th of June he is placed on a ventilator. Around the world, disciples, godbrothers and well-wishers begin to chant for his recovery.

events.title: Seven days of kīrtana, around the clock
events.body: While he lies on the ventilator, ISKCON’s Harināma Saṅkīrtana Ministry and ISKCON Ujjain call the world to chant for him — twenty-four hours a day for seven days without a break, concluding at midnight on the 26th of June. Devotees on every continent take their hour and pass the holy name on to the next. The man who had given his voice to the songs of surrender was now being sung for.

events.title: He departs this world
events.body: On the 29th of June his doctors report that he has become critically unwell; on the morning of the 4th of July they write that every remaining option has been exhausted. He departs a few hours later, at the age of seventy-four, with Śrīla Prabhupāda’s kīrtana playing beside him. ISKCON’s leadership calls it a great loss for the society and for the world; for thousands of disciples it is simply the loss of the shelter of their lives.

events.title: Samādhi at Śrīdhāma Māyāpur
events.body: On the 5th of July his sacred body is bathed, dressed and honoured in the United States; on the 10th it begins its final journey to India; and on the morning of the 13th of July it is placed in samādhi at Śrīdhāma Māyāpur — the holy dhāma where, forty-four years earlier, a young seeker back from the Himālayas had first joined the devotees of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

events.title: His samādhi mandira opens
events.body: On Nṛsiṁha-caturdaśī of 2021 his samādhi mandira at Māyāpur is opened — white Makrana marble, raised after the pattern of Śrīla Sanātana Gosvāmī’s samādhi in Vṛndāvana. It stands near the puṣpa-samādhi of Śrīla Prabhupāda: close, as he had always wished to be, to his spiritual master.
